Era 3, the alphabetical view -- the richest pre-2013 surface. Two columns: CURRENT holdings as Name, PRIOR holdings as bare text between

The anchor is deliberately non-capturing so both columns key on the NAME: era slugs drift across Battery's five site generations (portfolio/tejas.html -> company/tejas-networks/) while norm(name) is stable, and the build keys on norm(name).

Era 4, the WordPress logo wall. Cards are logo-only -- no alt text and no rendered name -- so the identity is the href slug and the row lands unnamed for the judge to name (COLLECTION.md 5, the logo-era rule). The class attribute also carries the firm's own sector-/stage-/status- filters; listing_regex drops them and the live site layer supplies those fields instead.

roster._note: Two people namespaces: /people/<slug>.html in the 2004-2012 site and /people/<first-last>/ from 2013. The 2008 site also grouped them behind generalpartners.html / partners.html / venturepartners.html / ips.html / operations.html, which are group pages, not people. Slugs are lowercase throughout, so First Round's capitalised-directory trap does not arise here; the namespace holds no founder directory.

site_api._note: Two surfaces, unioned. (1) battery.com is WordPress and answers /wp-json/wp/v2/types, but the `company` post type is NOT REST-exposed and the /company/ index loads over admin-ajax, so ladder step 1 fails and the rows come from 351 per-company detail fetches driven by the Yoast company sitemap -- scratch/pull-site-companies.py, saved as a file_list so the union stays reproducible. Those pages carry the firm's own SECTORS, INVESTED year, free-text STATUS, Location, STAGE (Early|Growth|Buyout) and the per-deal Battery Team. (2) /list-of-all-companies/ is the marketing-rule compliance list, 679 entries headed 'All investments as of Q1 2026' with no declared exclusions -- roughly double the portfolio surface and the only surface carrying the 1980s-90s book. site_entry_stage and invest_year are scored on the calibration gate before either labels a row.

edgar._note: Entity-qualified phrases only. Bare 'Battery' is unusable on EDGAR full-text search: it matches every lithium-battery issuer, every 'battery of tests' and Battery Park. The registered namesakes that share the word and are NOT this firm: Battery Park (Nomura CLO / high-yield vehicles, New York), Batterymarch (the Legg Mason quant shop), Battery Future Acquisition Corp (a SPAC), Battery Global Advisors LLC (CRD 158508, a separate active RIA at the same Boston tower, suite 1150, whose Alternative Income / Uncorrelated / Opportunity funds file from there), Battery Private Inc (CRD 284734, a d/b/a of Advisory Services Network), Battery East Group / Scenic Advisement, and a cluster of battery-metals miners.

desks._note: One adviser, one desk, no partition. Battery Management Corp. (CRD 160921, active RIA) is the whole firm, d/b/a Battery Ventures, with two RELYING advisers -- BMC UK Subadvisor Support Ltd and Battery Ventures Israel Ltd -- so the UK and Israel offices are IN under T1 exactly as LSVP's US/Europe/Israel offices are under CRD 160187. Crucially the firm runs early, growth AND buyout out of ONE fund family (Battery Ventures VI-XV, Side Funds, Select I-II), so the T1 strategy-desk addendum finds no separate vehicle to partition and desks.partition stays empty; the buyout book is separated at the TRANSACTION level by T3's control test instead. Excluded: Battery Global Advisors (its own RIA, CRD 158508, suite 1150 of the same tower -- the Accel-KKR / Lightspeed Faction pattern) and its Alternative Income / Uncorrelated / Opportunity funds; the Opportunities Access feeders, which file from 200 West Street, Goldman Sachs' address, and are third-party feeders (the Thrive IX Access precedent). Desks resolve by CIK and filing address, never the name pattern alone.

profile._note: focus_min_companies ~4.5% of the expected ~680-row base. Battery publishes its own five-sector vocabulary (Application Software, Infrastructure Software, Consumer, Industrial Tech, Life Science Tools), which stands until the base-derived tag coverage clears the 25% bar.

shape._note: Defaults kept at kickoff. Battery has invested since 1983 and its published list runs to 679 names, most of them 1990s and 2000s enterprise-infrastructure companies, so the $1B share should sit well under the guard.

commoncrawl._note: The layer's job here is 2017-2021, between the logo-wall era's last good captures and the current site, and as the standing fallback if the Internet Archive goes down mid-run.
